# fakecloud_iam::persistence - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-iam/0.31.0/fakecloud_iam/persistence/index.html

## Expand description

Shared IAM snapshot persistence.

Both `IamService` and `StsService` operate on the same `SharedIamState`
and therefore share a single on-disk snapshot. The save routine and the
serializing Mutex live here so both services route through the same
critical section.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [new_](https://docs.rs/fn.new_snapshot_lock.html)- snapshot_ - lock
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_iam_snapshot.html)- iam_ - snapshot
- Persist the current IAM state as a snapshot. Offloads the serde + blocking file write to the Tokio blocking pool so the async runtime stays responsive.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [IamSnapshot](https://docs.rs/type.IamSnapshotLock.html)- Lock
- Serializes concurrent snapshot writes across both IAM and STS services.
Without it, two tasks could clone state under the RwLock, serialize
independently, and race on `store.save()`, leaving older bytes as the final on-disk state.

---

# fakecloud_iam::policy_evaluator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-iam/0.31.0/fakecloud_iam/policy_evaluator/index.html

## Expand description

Adapter that implements [ fakecloud_core::auth::IamPolicyEvaluator](https://docs.rs/fakecloud-core/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/fakecloud_core/auth/trait.IamPolicyEvaluator.html)
over the shared IAM state + Phase 1 evaluator.

Mirrors the shape of [ crate::credential_resolver](https://docs.rs/credential_resolver/index.html): the trait lives in

`fakecloud-core`, the concrete implementation lives here, and dispatch
calls through the trait so the dependency edge points core -> iam only.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [IamPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.IamPolicyEvaluatorImpl.html)- Evaluator - Impl
- `IamPolicyEvaluator`- `crate::state::IamState`

}## Expand description

Abstraction over “given a principal, an action, and request-time
condition keys, say Allow / Deny”. Implemented by `fakecloud-iam`
against `IamState` + the evaluator. Dispatch calls this for every
request when `FAKECLOUD_IAM != off` and the target service opts in.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_core/auth.rs.html#403-410)#### fn [evaluate](https://docs.rs#tymethod.evaluate)(

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_core/auth.rs.html#403-410)

#### fn [evaluate](https://docs.rs#tymethod.evaluate)(
    &self,
    principal: &[Principal](https://docs.rs/struct.Principal.html),
    action: &[IamAction](https://docs.rs/struct.IamAction.html),
    context: &[ConditionContext](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionContext.html),
    session_policies: &[[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)],
    scps: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)]>,
) -> [IamDecision](https://docs.rs/enum.IamDecision.html)

Evaluate `action` against the identity policies attached to
`principal`, using `context` for `Condition` block resolution.
`session_policies` are the raw JSON session-policy documents
from the STS call that minted the caller’s credential (empty
for IAM user access keys). `scps` are the inherited SCP
documents (root-OU first, account-direct last) that form the
top-of-chain allow-list ceiling; `None` means no org exists
for this principal or the principal is exempt (management,
service-linked role) and the layer is a pass-through.

    resource_account_id: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    session_policies: &[[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)],

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_core/auth.rs.html#439-446)#### fn [evaluate_anonymous](https://docs.rs#method.evaluate_anonymous)(
    &self,
    _action: &[IamAction](https://docs.rs/struct.IamAction.html),
    _context: &[ConditionContext](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionContext.html),
    _resource_policy_json: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
) -> [IamDecision](https://docs.rs/enum.IamDecision.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_core/auth.rs.html#439-446)

#### fn [evaluate_anonymous](https://docs.rs#method.evaluate_anonymous)(
    &self,
    _action: &[IamAction](https://docs.rs/struct.IamAction.html),
    _context: &[ConditionContext](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionContext.html),
    _resource_policy_json: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
) -> [IamDecision](https://docs.rs/enum.IamDecision.html)

Evaluate `action` for an **anonymous** (unsigned) caller against a
resource-based policy in isolation. Anonymous requests carry no
identity, so the resource policy is the sole authorization source:
the request is allowed only if the policy explicitly grants the
action to a wildcard principal (`Principal:"*"` / `{"AWS":"*"}`).

`resource_policy_json` is the raw policy document (S3 bucket policy
today); `None` or a non-public policy yields [ IamDecision::ImplicitDeny](https://docs.rs/enum.IamDecision.html#variant.ImplicitDeny).
ACL-based public grants are evaluated separately by the dispatcher
via

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.ResourcePolicyProvider.html#method.public_acl_allows)

`ResourcePolicyProvider::public_acl_allows`The default implementation returns [ IamDecision::ImplicitDeny](https://docs.rs/enum.IamDecision.html#variant.ImplicitDeny) so
evaluators that don’t support anonymous access never silently grant.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# fakecloud_iam::resource_policy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-iam/0.31.0/fakecloud_iam/resource_policy/index.html

## Expand description

STS implementation of [ ResourcePolicyProvider](https://docs.rs/fakecloud-core/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/fakecloud_core/auth/trait.ResourcePolicyProvider.html).

For `sts:AssumeRole*`, the “resource policy” is the role’s trust
policy (`assume_role_policy_document`). This provider looks up the
role by ARN in the target account’s IAM state and returns the trust
policy document so the cross-account evaluator can apply the correct
`identity AND resource` semantics.

---
